messages.author: 94d3628bc0835e1b
messages.subject: similar htseq-count command line
parts:
-Hi,

I was using htseq-count with this command line:

htseq-count -f bam -r pos -a 27 -m intersection-strict --stranded=no -t exon -i exon_id input.bam GRCh37.gtf > counts_exons.txt


do you think that the similar command with featureCounts could be:

featureCounts -p -f -Q 27 -T 10 -t exon -g 'exon_id' -a GRCh37.gtf -o counts_exons.txt input.bam

thank you for your help --

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: similar htseq-count command line
parts:
I think htseq-count and featureCounts will give you same counting results for most of the reads with your provided settings.

But featureCounts will not count the following read but htseq-count will assign the read to exon 1:


Read                          RRRRRRRRRR
Exon 1        EEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE
Exon 2                                  EEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE


featureCounts will assign the following read to Exon 1 but htseq-count will not:

Read                          RRRRRRRR
Exon 1       EEEEEEEEEEEE

messages.author: 94d3628bc0835e1b
messages.subject: Re: similar htseq-count command line
parts:
yes i understand,
featureCounts avoid to count when there are ambiguity assignment on multiple exons, don"t you ?

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: similar htseq-count command line
parts:
Yes that is correct, although you can instruct featureCounts to assign a read to all its overlapping exons by specifying '-O' option.

Also note that if you summarize reads to genes (your command summarized reads to exons not genes), a read overlapping multiple exons from the same gene will be counted and counted only once for that gene.

Wei

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: similar htseq-count command line
parts:
Hi Beth,

That is basically correct. But your command counts read pairs, which is inconsistent with the example you showed in which you count reads. Also, you use '-s 2' in your command (reversely complemented) but you did not show the strandness of reads in your example. I refined your example a bit to make it more clearer:

featureCounts  -a gtf_file -o output1 -F GTF -t exon -g gene_id -s 2 -C -T 10 bam_file


 

+ Strand  Read1                          RRRRRRRRRR

+ Strand  Gene 1 Exon 1        EEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE
-  Strand  Gene 2 Exon 2                                  EEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE

- Strand   Read2                                                  RRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR


The counting results will be that Read1 is assigned to Gene2 and Read2 is assigned to Gene 1, regardless whether you turned on '-O' option or not.

Best,
Wei
